tasks.task: Write a radio or streaming audio ad timed to the second

items.when: When air time is booked and you need the steps from brief to approved script in order
When you need a 15, 30 or 60 second script with sound cues, voice notes and legal lines
Before you pick an opening, to get ten different first lines, each with the line that follows
When a funny spot is nearly there and every spare word has to go
When the script is drafted, to find every line that trips the tongue and fix it

tasks.task: Write a podcast host-read ad

items.when: Before writing, to put the listener's situation and doubts in their own words
When a host will read the ad and needs talking points, must-say lines and a loose script
When the read needs a way in, to get ten openings the host could say naturally
Before sending to the host, to catch lines that sound written, not spoken
Before the sponsor signs off, to catch claims the host should not make

tasks.task: Write copy for a flyer or poster

items.when: Before any words, to cut the job to one idea, one feeling and one thing to show
When you know the size and where it will be seen and need the copy written to fit
When you need twenty or more headlines sorted by type to choose from
When it is an event poster and you want a guided run to checked text and a layout
When you have a long list of headlines, to score each read alone and keep the best three
When the layout is drafted, to see where the eye lands first and what to cut

tasks.task: Write a tri-fold or multi-page brochure

items.when: Before writing panels, to put the selling points in the order a buyer needs them
When you need copy written panel by panel to the fold and the word count
When the cover panel needs several headline angles to choose from
When the client's draft is a wall of text, to name the main idea and cut what fights it
When the brochure is drafted, to tighten it in passes for clarity, proof and the ask

tasks.task: Write a billboard, bus shelter or vehicle line

items.when: Before writing, to find the one thought a driver can take in at a glance
When you need a line of seven words or fewer written for the viewing distance
When you need five short lines, each from a different angle, with word counts
When the line is safe and forgettable and needs one bold picture and words joined
Before it goes to print or live, to test whether it reads in two seconds

tasks.task: Write a newspaper or magazine ad

items.when: When you need five headlines from different angles, with a fair plan to test them
When the ad must persuade with checked facts and not adjectives
When the body copy is vague and needs one clear promise and facts that back it
When the headline is chosen, to check it picks the right reader and promises a reward
When the ad is laid out, to check the path from picture to headline to coupon

tasks.task: Plan a direct mail campaign and its break-even

items.when: When a mail drop is planned and you need the cycle from list and offer to readout
When you need the break-even response rate, list rules, offer and tracking planned
When the client wants to mail everyone at once, to set a small test and a rollout rule
When an online brand mails its own customers after set triggers like a lapsed order
When the offer is weak, to add honest limits, a deadline, a bonus and a guarantee
When the plan is all creative and no numbers, to bring it back to offer, list and test
Before printing, to score the offer, price and guarantee and get three changes to test

tasks.task: Write a postcard or sales letter in three versions

items.when: When it is a letter, to outline it from the research with the proof each part needs
When you need postcard or letter copy in three versions, each with its own code
When each version needs a different kind of headline: self-interest, news or curiosity
When the letter reads like a company wrote it and should sound like one person
When the piece has a reply coupon or form, to make it sell the offer and ask less
When envelope, letter and offer are drafted, to review the whole package before print

tasks.task: Set up tracking per version and read the response counts

items.when: When responses are in and you need to log them, compare versions and plan the next drop
When each version needs its own tagged web link or QR code address
When two versions will be mailed, to change one thing only and key each one
When you have counts for two versions, to see the gap and whether luck explains it

tasks.task: Write jingle lyrics with a melody guide

items.when: When you need original lyrics with syllable counts, rhyme and 15, 30 and 60 second cuts
When the hook line is flat, to get three versions people are more likely to remember
When the jingle will run under a short video and needs a script and a music brief
When the client wants to hear a rough demo, to write the music tool prompt
When you want two or three rough sung demos so the client can compare hooks
When the jingle is drafted, to score how well the tune and line could become known

tasks.task: Brief a sonic logo, podcast intro or brand music

items.when: When a composer needs a written brief for a short sound mark, intro or outro
When you need a music bed described by genre, tempo and instruments
When the client cannot picture the sound, to make short sample tracks to react to

tasks.task: Write a voiceover script for a video

items.when: When the words are heard, not read, and must fit an exact running time
Before drafting, to compare four kinds of video script with an opening for each
When the script is drafted, to find each weak line and get a fix
When the client needs a finished voice read from the approved script

tasks.task: Adapt a script or ad for another language

items.when: When the script must read naturally in the new language with local tone
When one approved script needs spoken versions and subtitles in several languages

tasks.task: Write a back cover blurb and store description

items.when: When you need blurb, store description, taglines and bios with no spoilers
When the first line of the blurb is flat, to get ten different ways in
Before publishing, to catch praise or claims about the book that nobody can back

tasks.task: Write an author bio in three lengths or a series page

items.when: When the author needs short, medium and long bios that match the book's tone
When the bio is a dry list, to add one or two sharp, true lines
Before it goes on the cover or store page, to fix slips and keep the author's voice

tasks.task: Write launch emails and pitches to reviewers and podcasts

items.when: When the author has a reader list and a launch date and needs the emails planned
When the plan is agreed and you need each email with subject lines and timing
When the book needs a list of reviewers and shows, pitch emails and a press kit outline
When a pitch goes to someone who has never heard of the author and must land fast
Before sending, to flag lines in the emails that could mislead or break the rules

tasks.task: Write and test a tagline or slogan

items.when: When the brand has no set messages and needs a tagline with proof points behind it
When you have a line that is right but dull, to get three versions that stick
When every line sounds like the category and you need a human angle
When you have candidates, to score each on ten tests and get sharper versions
When the line makes a claim, to check it is true, specific and not a rival's too

tasks.task: Write search and social ad lines to the character limits

items.when: When you need Google headlines and descriptions or Meta text that fit the limits
When one idea works and you need ten or more different angles with hooks
Before launch, to check Facebook or Instagram ads against the platform's ad rules

tasks.task: Check claims and wording before an ad goes out

items.when: Before any ad goes out, to catch wording that could mislead or be rejected
When the client has proof on file, to pair every claim with it and show the gaps
When there is no proof file yet, to sort each claim as fine, needs proof or cut
When a prize draw, discount or promotion must follow the law where it runs

tasks.task: Find the one campaign idea and write the copy brief

items.when: When one campaign runs across print, outdoor, audio or mail and needs one plan
When notes are scattered, to get a one-page brief with the one thing to say
When the brand has no clear claim, to get three to five one-sentence claims to pick from
When you need concepts from seven different groups, with the best eight ranked
When the idea is chosen, to score how well it can get noticed and remembered

tasks.task: Review a current print piece and rank the fixes

items.when: When the client sends a layout, to see where the eye goes and what is in the way
When the copy must bring a response, to get a critique and fixes for the weakest parts
When the headline is the likely problem, to test who it picks and what it promises

tasks.task: Plan the offer and wording for a local promotion

items.when: When a sale is planned, to pick an offer the margins allow and a true deadline
When the client wants more than a price cut: a gift, bundle or pre-order offer
When you must choose percent or amount off and the words for the sign or flyer
When choosing between print, radio and outdoor, to plan one small test with its costs

tasks.task: Write a trade show leave-behind or one-page sales sheet

items.when: Before writing, to rank the features as selling points and flag claims needing proof
When a buyer or deal needs a one-pager, objection sheet or short pitch outline
When the sheet needs a headline, to compare five angles side by side
When the sheet tries to say everything, to cut it to one idea a stand visitor keeps

always.when: Before any work for a client with a live site, to capture their voice, facts and prices
When a draft is done, to fix off-brand words without touching the claims
When copy states facts or numbers, to check each against a trusted source
Before delivery, to catch stock phrases that make copy read as machine written
Last step before sign-off, to catch spelling and grammar slips with a log of changes
Before hand-over, so a fresh reader takes the client's seat and lists what fails the brief

helpers.when: When the copy needs a print layout, a poster design or printer-ready files
When an ad or voiceover must work in another language and market
When the ad sends people to a landing page that must carry on the same promise
When response counts across several drops or channels need a proper readout
When a book or campaign needs press coverage, not only pitch emails
When a host read, intro or audio ad needs recording, editing and show planning

gaps: No library item writes radio or audio-only ad scripts; apart from the kit skill, every script writer is for video
No library item makes or compares billboard and outdoor lines; the options come from general headline writers
No library item writes book blurbs, author bios or series pages, or checks a blurb for spoilers and genre fit
No library item plans a brochure panel by panel for a given fold
No library item checks jingle lyrics for singability, stress and rhyme, or for likeness to an existing tune
No library item adapts an ad for another language and re-times it; the translator skill does not check running time
No library item writes shelf signs or point-of-sale copy
No library item sets up phone call tracking or unique codes for offline ads; the link tracker covers web links only
No library item works out a break-even response rate for mail; the break-even tools are built for online ad spend
The sonic logo brief has no check item; nothing in the library reviews a music brief before it goes to a composer
